title: Add us-east Streaming health panels (disconnects, first-token latency, 5xx) for status validation
author: Aisha Bello
description: Context: During the 2025-11-07 us-east streaming degradation we struggled to quickly answer “is this a streaming-only issue or broader Hosted API impact?” and we ended up hesitating on which public status components to mark impacted. This PR adds a small set of focused, region-aware panels for Streaming in us-east that on-call can use to validate streaming-specific degradations before posting status page updates. What’s included: (1) a new “Streaming (us-east)” section in the Hosted API component dashboard with panels for streaming disconnect rate, stream error rate (gateway 5xx + upstream), first-token latency p95/p99, and active stream concurrency; (2) a side-by-side comparison row (Streaming vs Non-streaming chat completions) to help confirm capability-scoped impact; (3) dashboard annotations that link to the status page update runbook and specify the “post-update confidence check” items (verify error + disconnect + first-token latency). Notes: Panels intentionally avoid customer identifiers and aggregate at component_id/region/capability. Thresholds are NOT alerting thresholds in this PR; they’re visualization defaults only (alert tuning happens in ENG-4841 / slo-toolkit). Testing/validation: Replayed a slice of the 2025-11-07 incident window against staging metrics and verified the panels light up as expected; also sanity-checked that non-streaming endpoints remain flat in the comparison row. Follow-ups: replicate panels for eu-west and ap-southeast once the region-aware streaming counters land in the redwood repo; we can also add a “status component tag” filter once pr-19211 label standardization is fully rolled out.
commits: dashboards: add streaming-us-east dashboard section + layout
metrics: add queries for disconnect_rate and stream_error_rate by capability
docs: link dashboard panels to status page update runbook + taxonomy
chore: rename panels to match status component naming conventions
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we make sure these queries are capability-scoped and don’t accidentally include websocket auth failures that are not customer-impacting? Also would be helpful to add an explicit “comparison” panel so on-call can quickly confirm it’s streaming-only. Aisha Bello (author): Updated streaming_error_rate to use gateway route tags for streaming-only endpoints and excluded authn/authz error classes. Added a comparison row: streaming first-token p95 vs non-streaming chat p95 in the same time window and a paired 5xx rate panel. Christine Wong (review): Please add a link/annotation to the status page runbook from the dashboard. The goal is that Comms Lead can use this dashboard as part of the verification step. Aisha Bello (author): Added dashboard annotations and a short panel description block with “confidence check” steps + runbook link. Caleb Johnson (review): These queries are a bit heavy; do we need the p99 and p95 both? And can we pin the timegrain? Aisha Bello (author): Dropped one redundant panel (kept p95 + p99 only for first-token latency), pinned to 1m rollups, and added $__interval overrides to reduce query fanout. Allison Grant (final): Looks good. Please ensure the titles use the same casing as the public component labels (Streaming, us-east). Approved.
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds us-east streaming health panels to validate streaming-specific degradations prior to status page updates; includes comparison panels to distinguish streaming vs non-streaming impact.
